title: Constrained Extensions with where

docs.title: Generics — Extensions with a Generic Where Clause

hints: An extension can apply only when `Element` meets a constraint.
Write one extension for `Element: BinaryInteger` and one for `Element: BinaryFloatingPoint`, each with its own `average`.
jsBridge: `extension Collection where Element: BinaryInteger` adds `average` only to collections of integers, a **constrained extension**. TS can't add methods conditionally to `Array<number>` without declaration merging hacks.

compass.q: How would you add `.average()` only to `number[]` in TS? Why is it awkward?
Two constrained extensions both apply (a type that's both integer and floating point, hypothetically): which wins?
Constrained extension vs free generic function `average<C: Collection>(_:)`: which is more discoverable?
`Array where Element == String` extensions are common. What's the risk of too many?
